title: The End Times Revealed
overview: Daniel Chapter 12 unveils prophetic revelations concerning the end times, focusing on deliverance, resurrection, and final judgment. It highlights the role of Michael, the great prince, who stands for God's people during unprecedented tribulation. The chapter promises resurrection to everlasting life or shame, emphasizing the destiny of the wise and righteous. It instructs Daniel to seal the prophecy until the time of the end, when knowledge will increase and understanding will be granted to the wise. The chapter concludes with specific timeframes for the fulfillment of these events, encouraging patient endurance and faithfulness. This chapter serves as a climactic conclusion to Daniel’s visions, offering hope and assurance of God’s sovereign control over history and the ultimate triumph of His people.
structure:
**Verses 1-3: The Time of Trouble and Resurrection.** Michael arises to protect God's people during unparalleled distress, followed by the promise of resurrection and eternal destinies for the wise and righteous.

**Verses 4-7: Sealing the Prophecy and the Question of Duration.** Daniel is commanded to seal the words until the end times, while a heavenly figure swears to the appointed period of tribulation and the scattering of the holy people.

**Verses 8-10: Daniel’s Inquiry and the Revelation of Understanding.** Daniel expresses confusion and seeks clarity, receiving assurance that the words remain sealed until the end, but the wise will ultimately understand.

**Verses 11-12: Specific Time Periods Given.** The removal of the daily sacrifice and the setting up of the abomination of desolation mark a period of 1290 days, with blessing promised to those who endure to 1335 days.

**Verse 13: The Final Exhortation.** Daniel is told to rest until the end, when he will rise to receive his allotted inheritance, closing the prophetic message with a note of hope and reward.

keyVerses.text: And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.
keyVerses.significance: This verse introduces Michael as the protector of God's people during unparalleled tribulation, affirming God's sovereign intervention and the deliverance of those whose names are recorded in the book of life, underscoring divine justice and salvation.

keyVerses.text: And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
keyVerses.significance: This verse explicitly teaches the resurrection of the dead, a foundational Christian doctrine, distinguishing eternal destinies based on righteousness, and highlighting the final judgment.

keyVerses.text: But thou, O Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end: many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall be increased.
keyVerses.significance: Daniel is commanded to seal the prophecy until the end times, indicating that full understanding is reserved for the future, while the increase of knowledge signals the approaching fulfillment of these prophetic events.

keyVerses.text: Many shall be purified, and made white, and tried; but the wicked shall do wickedly: and none of the wicked shall understand; but the wise shall understand.
keyVerses.significance: This verse contrasts the destiny of the righteous and the wicked, emphasizing spiritual purification and discernment granted to the wise, reinforcing the theme of divine justice and revelation.

keyVerses.text: But go thou thy way till the end be: for thou shalt rest, and stand in thy lot at the end of the days.
keyVerses.significance: The final verse offers comfort and assurance to Daniel and believers, promising rest in death and a future resurrection to receive their inheritance, affirming hope beyond present trials.

characters.name: Michael
characters.description: Described as the great prince who stands for the children of Daniel’s people, Michael is a heavenly protector and leader during the time of unprecedented tribulation, symbolizing God’s divine intervention on behalf of His people.

characters.name: Daniel
characters.description: The prophet receiving and recording the visions, Daniel is instructed to seal the prophecy until the time of the end. His role includes inquiry and faithful reception of divine revelation despite initial lack of understanding.

characters.name: Man Clothed in Linen
characters.description: A heavenly figure standing upon the waters of the river who swears by the eternal God concerning the duration of the tribulation period, serving as a divine messenger revealing the timeline of end-time events.

themes.description: The chapter emphasizes God’s protection through Michael during unparalleled tribulation, assuring believers of ultimate deliverance, reflecting the biblical theme of God’s sovereignty over history and His care for His people.

Daniel 12 clearly teaches the resurrection of the dead with eternal destinies, a cornerstone of Christian eschatology, affirming that the righteous will receive everlasting life while the wicked face eternal contempt.

The command to seal the prophecy until the end highlights the progressive unfolding of divine revelation, showing that understanding is granted in God’s timing, which encourages faithfulness amid uncertainty.
The chapter encourages believers to patiently endure trials and wait for God’s promises, offering blessing to those who persevere to the end, reinforcing the biblical call to steadfastness in faith.

historicalContext:
Daniel was written during or shortly after the Babylonian exile (6th century BC), a time of great upheaval for the Jewish people. The geopolitical landscape was dominated by empires such as Babylon and later Persia, with Jewish exiles longing for restoration and deliverance. The customs included temple worship with daily sacrifices, which are referenced in the chapter’s prophetic timeline. The political situation involved oppression and persecution, making the promises of divine protection and ultimate justice especially poignant for Daniel’s audience.

Understanding the apocalyptic genre and Jewish eschatological expectations of the time helps clarify the symbolic language and time periods mentioned. The chapter reflects hope amid suffering and anticipates God’s final intervention to establish His eternal kingdom, a message that resonated deeply with a people under foreign domination and awaiting Messiah’s coming.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology sees Daniel 12 as affirming the resurrection of the body and final judgment, emphasizing God’s sovereign control over history and the certainty of Christ’s return. The sealed prophecy points to the progressive unfolding of God’s redemptive plan culminating in the new heavens and new earth.

Dispensationalists interpret the time periods literally, associating the tribulation with a future seven-year period before Christ’s second coming. Michael is viewed as a preeminent angelic warrior protecting Israel, and the sealed prophecy is to be unsealed in the last days as knowledge increases.

Early church interpreters often saw Michael as a type of Christ or a chief angelic figure, with the resurrection and judgment passages affirming Christian hope in life after death. The sealing of the book was understood as God’s sovereign timing for revealing mysteries to the church.

crossReferences.connection: Jesus teaches about the resurrection of the dead to eternal life or judgment, paralleling Daniel 12’s promise of awakening to everlasting destinies.
The final judgment scene in Revelation echoes Daniel’s depiction of resurrection and judgment based on deeds and righteousness.
Paul’s teaching on the resurrection at the last trumpet complements Daniel’s prophecy of the dead awakening at the end of days.
Jesus describes a time of unprecedented tribulation similar to Daniel’s time of trouble, affirming the prophetic consistency.
The concept of appointed times and seasons aligns with Daniel’s emphasis on God’s sovereign timing for the end.

application: Trust God’s sovereign protection during times of personal or communal trial, knowing He stands for His people as Michael did.
Live with the hope of resurrection and eternal life, allowing this assurance to shape daily decisions and priorities.
Seek wisdom and understanding through prayer and study, recognizing that God grants insight to the faithful in His timing.
Persevere in faith and obedience, especially when facing persecution or hardship, remembering the blessing promised to those who endure.
Embrace the call to righteousness by influencing others toward godly living, shining as stars in a dark world.
Rest in God’s promises about the future, allowing this hope to bring peace amid uncertainty and suffering.
conclusion: Daniel 12 stands as a powerful conclusion to the prophet’s visions, offering believers assurance of God’s ultimate victory over evil, the reality of resurrection, and the certainty of final judgment. It calls for faithfulness amid trials, promising deliverance and blessing to the wise and righteous. This chapter encourages Christians to live with hope, wisdom, and endurance, confident that God’s sovereign plan will unfold perfectly in His appointed time.
timeline: c. 6th century BC - Babylonian Exile and Early Persian Period
